assumptions.label: Loan growth
assumptions.basis: The FY2025A base is the derived 31-Dec-2025 book of Rp895,5tn (F46: sustainable financing of Rp197tn at 22% of total credit), cross-checked at Rp898,9tn by the Rp17,079tn December NPL at a 1,9% ratio (F54). From that base the book reached Rp992,5tn at 30-Sep-2026 (+22,2% yoy, S3) but the quarterly pace has decelerated from +8,2% in the first half (Rp895,5tn to Rp968,5tn, S16) to +2,5% in the third quarter; management's raised 10-13% FY2026 target (S19) therefore implies a fourth quarter close to flat against an exceptional fourth-quarter 2025 step, and the top of that range is the most likely full-year outturn, about Rp1.012tn. Growth then eases to 11,5%, 9%, 7% and 6% and to 4,5% in perpetuity, the retention-funded rate at a 12% ROE and a 65% payout, once the one-off fourth-quarter base effect is behind us.

assumptions.label: Deposit growth
assumptions.basis: The December 2025 DPK level is not disclosed by any reachable source, so it is assumed: the Rp895,5tn December loan book (F46) at the 87,9% loan-to-deposit ratio (F39) gives Rp1.018,7tn (F47). The 87,9% is the 30-Sep-2026 print applied to a 31-Dec-2025 balance sheet, and the alternative route through the September-2026 DPK share of liabilities (86,0% applied to end-2025 liabilities of Rp1.185,72tn, S12) is the same September ratio under a second divisor, not an independent confirmation. Deposits enter no revenue line - net interest income is the margin on earning assets - so the level only sets the displayed LDR. DPK then reached Rp1.124,59tn at 30-Sep-2026, +20,36% yoy [S2], and the September 2025 stock of Rp934,33tn [S22] is the prior-year comparative, not the opening balance. Deposit growth is held level with loan growth from that corrected base so the modelled LDR stays at the 88,0% the bank actually printed, and CASA of Rp733,7tn growing 19,6% [S4] keeps the mix stable: 65,2% of DPK at September 2026.

assumptions.label: Earning assets / loans
assumptions.basis: The ratio is the one the bank's own reported margin implies, not an assumed balance sheet. Annualised nine-month net interest income is Rp44,3tn [S2] and the reported margin is 3,5% [S4], which put earning assets near Rp1.266tn against average loans of about Rp966tn over the same nine months, or 1,31x. Applied to average loans of Rp953,7tn over FY2026E that reproduces NII of about Rp44,4tn on the bank's own numbers. It is also consistent with the balance sheet: total assets of Rp1.362,05tn at end-2025 [S12] mean 86% of assets earn interest, the rest being cash, fixed assets and intangibles. The ratio then rises to 1,33 by FY2030E as the rupiah statutory reserve requirement falls from 9% to 7% [S10], which releases about 2pp of deposits from required reserves into earning assets; the release is phased from November 2026, so only a fifth of it lands in FY2026E.

assumptions.label: Net interest margin
assumptions.basis: Level, not trend. The bank reports a 3,5% margin for nine months of 2026, 30bp lower yoy [S4], with the loan yield down to 6,9% from 7,3% [S24] and the cost of funds down to 2,77% from 2,83% [S4]: a realised deposit beta of about 0,15 on a 40bp fall in the asset yield, because the policy rate was held at 5,75% [S2] and only part of the deposit book repriced. On this model's wider earning base (1,31x loans rather than the bank's own aggregate) a 3,55% margin reproduces the reported nine-month NII of Rp33,24tn [S2] annualised, and 3,5% on the bank's base is the same number: the two bases differ by about 1%. The path is then held flat at 3,55% through FY2030E and in perpetuity, with no recovery in it at any point: the level stays below the 3,8% the bank earned a year ago [S4], and CASA of 65,2% of DPK [S4] and a 0,15 realised beta support the margin without restoring it. The sector deck's warning that rate-sensitive Indonesian bank margins are impaired [S0] is adopted rather than argued with, which is why the input never rises back toward the pre-2026 level.

assumptions.label: Non-interest income growth
assumptions.basis: Definition first: the model's non-interest line comes from the data pack at Rp17,58tn for FY2025 [S0] and is narrower than the Rp24,6tn of non-interest income the company reports [S14], because the company total includes treasury and securities results that are not fee income. The pack line tracks fee-based income: the bank printed Rp13,9tn of fee-based income in nine months of 2026, +8,3% [S24], which annualises to Rp18,5tn, about 5% above the pack line. FY2026E growth is therefore set at the 8,3% the bank printed rather than at a view, easing to 8% in perpetuity as transaction volumes scale (wondr users +58% to 16,6 million [S4]); no fee-led re-rating is assumed.

assumptions.label: Cost-to-income
assumptions.basis: This ratio is a modelling device and is not comparable with the bank's own cost-to-income ratio, which was 47,3% for nine months of 2026 (revenue of Rp51,15tn against operating expenses of Rp24,20tn [S13]) and which the model cannot reproduce because the data pack's non-interest line is the narrower fee-based one (C3 of the review: FY2026E revenue and opex were nine-month run-rates, and the modelled CTI was compared with the company's). The input is therefore set so that PPOP, the line the valuation actually depends on, reproduces the bank's own: reported PPOP of Rp27,53tn in nine months [S13] annualises to about Rp36,7tn, which on the pack's narrower revenue of Rp63,3tn is a 42,1% ratio. The arithmetic closes on both sides: the modelled revenue is about Rp5,3tn narrower than the bank's and the modelled cost base about Rp5,6tn narrower, so the difference is definitional and cancels in PPOP. Only a gradual improvement to 40,3% by FY2030E is assumed, because operating expenses grew 12% against 11,6% PPOP growth [S13].

assumptions.label: Credit cost
assumptions.basis: Derived from the reported lines rather than read off a provisions disclosure the pack does not carry. Nine months of 2026: PPOP of Rp27,53tn [S13] less PBT of about Rp19,8tn (attributable profit Rp16,12tn [S22] grossed up for minorities and the 17,9% effective tax rate) leaves about Rp7,75tn of provisions, or Rp10,3tn annualised, which on average loans of about Rp944,0tn is 1,09%. FY2025 was 1,16% on the same arithmetic. FY2026E is set at that run-rate, 1,08%, and eases to 1,00% by FY2029E on the improvement the bank reports: total reserves are 3,8% of loans against the industry's 3,5% [S3], NPL coverage is 193,3% [S3] and LaR has fallen from 10,4% to 7,8% [S4]. The 1,00% through-cycle anchor is above the 0,5-0,8% that cleaner peers run, which is deliberate: wholesale is 68% of the book and grew 30,3% [S15], so the vintage has to season. It is below the 1,15% carried in perpetuity before this revision, which was the red team's point.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 actual of 65% (Rp13,03tn of a Rp20,04tn attributable profit, F28/F25), not at the top of the 60-85% SOE band in VAL_BANKS, and the reason is capital rather than a view on state fiscal need: at a 12% ROE a 65% payout retains 4,2% of equity a year against a loan book growing 13%, so the ratio drifts from the 20,7% of end-2025 (F27) to the 19,2% the bank actually printed in September 2026 (F38) and to about 18% by FY2028E on this model. A 75% payout would remove another 1,3pp of that path and force slower growth, which is why the band top is carried in the bull case rather than the base (C8 of the review). The dividend is the return a shareholder actually receives while the multiple stays below book, so the payout is not used as a valuation lever.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: The board has approval to buy back up to Rp905,48bn following the March 2026 annual meeting [S11] and announced a tranche of up to Rp547bn running from 28 October 2026 to 27 January 2027 [S7]. At the current price the announced tranche is 0,44% of the 37,283m shares; we assume roughly two-thirds of it executes inside the financial year, so FY2026E carries a 0,3% reduction and the count is held flat after that. No rights issue is modelled in the base case: at 0,69x book an issue would be book-value dilutive per share, and the capital is funded from retention on the path shown in the payout note.

assumptions.label: RWA / loans
assumptions.basis: The latest disclosure puts CAR at 19.2% on 30-Sep-2026 [S24] against total equity of Rp174.26tn [S12] and loans of Rp992.5tn [S3], which implies RWA near Rp908tn, or 0,91x the loan book. The model holds 0,92, the small difference being the rising risk weight of a book whose wholesale segment is growing 30,3% [S15]. Holding it flat keeps the modelled capital ratio close to the reported level as the book grows, and the fall from 20.7% a year earlier [S6] is the headroom the raised loan target is spending.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth
assumptions.basis: 4,0% nominal sits below the 5,0% IDR terminal cap and below g = ROE x (1 - payout) of about 4,2% at a 12,0% sustainable ROE and a 65% payout, so perpetual growth never outruns retention-funded capital growth. It reflects the long-run inflation path underpinning a BI rate held at 5,75% [S2] plus modest real growth, not extrapolation of the current credit cycle.

challenges.section: 3. Financial analysis and forecasts / fund record loan_growth, deposit_growth
challenges.challenge: F1 (loans 812,200, period FY2025A) and F6 (deposits 934,330, period FY2025A) are 30-Sep-2025 stocks, not 31-Dec-2025 balances: the F1 quote itself says "periode yang sama tahun sebelumnya sebesar Rp 812,2 triliun" (S15). The report's claim that no reachable source discloses the December-2025 level is false on its own evidence: S14 says sustainable financing of Rp197tn was "setara 22% dari total kredit BNI" in 2025, implying total credit of ~Rp895tn (range Rp876-916tn at 21.5-22.5%), and that cross-checks with the 15.9% FY2025 growth in S6/S14/S17/S18 (Dec-2024 ~Rp773tn x 1.159 = ~Rp896tn). On that base FY2026E loans of Rp1,043.7tn are +16.5% (range +13.9% to +19.2%), not +28.5%, so "we take that at face value" is not what the model does, and "growth rates are unaffected" is wrong: a Sep-2025-to-Dec-2026 rate contains two Q4 steps. The same period break makes FY2025A earning assets 1.68x loans and FY2026E 1.31x, which is the base the NIM plug is fitted to.
challenges.answer: Accepted and rebuilt on the 31-Dec-2025 anchors. Loans are now F46 = Rp895,455bn (sustainable financing of Rp197tn stated as 22% of total credit, S14) and deposits F47 = Rp1,018,700bn (that book at the reported 87,9% LDR, S24); F1 and F6 are retained only as 2025Q3 comparatives and relabelled as such. Earning assets were rebuilt on one definition (F37, the 1,31x implied by the reported margin) so FY2025A and FY2026E no longer sit on different bases. FY2026E growth is 13,0% rather than the review's 16,5%: the September book of Rp992,5tn is already +22,2% yoy (S3) but the quarterly pace decelerated to +2,5% in Q3, so reaching Rp1.043,7tn would need +5,2% in a single fourth quarter against an exceptional Q4-2025 step; the top of management's raised 10-13% band (S19) is the most likely outturn. The "no source discloses December" sentence now says the level is derived, not undisclosed, and "growth rates are unaffected" is deleted.

challenges.section: 3. Financial analysis and forecasts / fund record nim
challenges.challenge: The NIM input (3.26% FY2026E rising to 3.41% FY2030E) never reaches the 3.5% the bank reported for 9M-2026 (F9/S4), while §2 and §3 call 3.5% "closer to a floor than a mid-cycle level" and cost of funds is falling (2.83% to 2.77%, F10). The "narrower asset base" defence is the analyst's own construction, not a disclosed fact: the reported 3.5% on annualised NII of Rp44.3tn implies earning assets of ~Rp1,266tn, or 1.276x loans, not the 1.31x used. On a consistent base the model's interest income per rupiah of loans falls from 4.50% (FY2025A, Rp40.3tn/Rp895tn) to 4.26% (FY2026E) and 4.10% (FY2027E), against 4.47% actual annualised in 9M-2026 — a 40bp decline through the very trough the report says has been reached. No deposit beta or CASA/TD path is stated, although VAL_BANKS requires both.
challenges.answer: Accepted. ea_loans is now on one definition: the ratio implied by the bank's own margin (annualised 9M NII of Rp44,3tn at the reported 3,5% gives about Rp1.266tn of earning assets over about Rp966tn of average loans, or 1,31x, S2/S4), applied to FY2025A and the forecast alike (F37). The NIM input is 3,55%, within a few basis points of the reported 3,5% on that base, so the 24bp discount the review objected to is gone. The path is now flat rather than recovering: 3,55% through FY2030E, which is the sector deck's stance adopted rather than argued with, and the "floor" language in sections 2 and 3 was replaced by "holds". The deposit beta and CASA path are now stated: a realised beta of about 0,15 on the 40bp fall in loan yield (7,3% to 6,9%, S24) with cost of funds down only 6bp (2,83% to 2,77%, S4), CASA at 65,2% of DPK (S4) and held flat.

challenges.challenge: The FY2026E revenue and cost lines are nine-month run-rates, not annual forecasts. FY2026E NOII is Rp18.90tn against Rp17.91tn already booked in 9M-2026 (S12), implying Q4-2026 NOII of ~Rp1.0tn versus ~Rp7.9tn in Q4-2025 (S6 Rp24.6tn less S12 9M-2025 Rp16.67tn). FY2026E opex is Rp26.81tn against Rp24.20tn in 9M-2026 (F22/S13), implying Q4 opex of Rp2.6tn versus a 9M average of Rp8.1tn. The company's FY2025 revenue was Rp64.9tn (NII Rp40.3tn + non-interest Rp24.6tn, S6/S17), not the Rp57.9tn in the assumptions basis, and 9M-2026 opex/TOI is 24.20/51.15 = 47.3%, not the 42.3% the report prints. PPOP is right (Rp36.57tn vs Rp36.7tn annualised) only because the revenue and cost errors offset, so the CTI key input and the efficiency narrative are wrong even though NP is not.
challenges.answer: Accepted, and disclosed rather than plugged. The model keeps the data pack's narrower fee-based non-interest line (S0) and now says so in section 3 and in the cti basis: it is not the company's Rp24,6tn non-interest line (F48/S14), and the modelled 42,1% cost-to-income ratio is a device calibrated so PPOP reproduces the bank's own Rp36,7tn annualised from Rp27,53tn in nine months (S13), not a claim about the company's 47,3% (opex Rp24,20tn on revenue Rp51,15tn, S13). NOII growth is set at the 8,3% the bank printed on fee-based income of Rp13,9tn (S24), not a run-rate of the full company line; opex is derived from PPOP rather than run-rated. The arithmetic closes: the modelled revenue is about Rp5,3tn narrower and the modelled cost base about Rp5,6tn narrower, so the gap cancels in PPOP, and the report no longer compares its ratio with the company's.

challenges.challenge: COE is 11.85%, 60bp below the house band. VAL_BANKS pins COE = 10y local sovereign + ERP of 5.0-6.0%; the engine's rf is 7.45%, so the band gives 12.45-13.45%. The build nets the default spread out of rf (7.45% - 1.62%) and adds beta x (4.23% + 2.46%), with coe_premium = 0.0. The desk's own BBCA file uses coe_premium 0.006 and COE 12.45% on identical rf/ERP/CRP/beta inputs, so the difference is a choice, not a data difference. At COE 12.45% the justified P/B falls from 1.073 to 0.997 and the 12-month value falls ~10% (sensitivity grid: +0.5pp COE -> Rp5,351; +1.0pp -> Rp5,059). The BUY survives (~+73%), but the 88.7% does not.
challenges.answer: Accepted. valuation.coe_premium is set to 0,006, which on the engine's 7,45% risk-free rate gives a cost of equity of 12,45% - the floor of the VAL_BANKS band of local ten-year plus five to six per cent, and identical to the desk's BBCA build. The COC inputs and the ADTV/float are now cited to the deck/config and the datapack (S0), not to S23. All methods and all three scenarios were re-run: warranted multiple 1,0647x, primary value Rp4,851, v0 Rp5,392, target Rp5,674 and a return of +82,3%. The BUY survives and the 88,7% does not, which is the review's point. Both of the review's own COE sensitivities now sit inside the method rather than outside it.

challenges.challenge: The 88.7% is not an earnings forecast but a 12-month full closure of the valuation gap: v0 Rp5,542 is rolled forward at COE and the target assumes the stock goes from 0.69x to ~1.07x book within twelve months. The report names no re-rating catalyst (the catalysts are results, the AGM and monthly statistics) and does not say why the market's discount — which it concedes may be pricing state-directed lending and rupiah risk — closes on that schedule. Meanwhile the base case is cautious on every operating driver (NIM below the reported trough, credit cost above the run-rate, payout below peers, terminal g below retention-funded growth) and optimistic only on the discount rate; the two offset, so the target is close to right by accident rather than by a most-likely build.
challenges.answer: Accepted, by making the claim testable rather than by re-scoping it away. Section 5 now says the target is a re-rating, names the mechanism (a dividend yield of 11,4% against a 12,45% cost of equity, so the multiple only has to stop falling, S11/S0) and the dated catalysts inside the window (full-year results, the March AGM dividend, the phased reserve-requirement release, S19/S11/S10), and states that the probability of full closure within twelve months is about the bull weight, one quarter. On the conservatism: the base now runs the top of the raised guidance, the derived credit-cost run-rate, the actual 65% payout and a flat margin, with the cost of equity at the band floor rather than below it, so the operating assumptions and the discount rate no longer offset each other - the discount rate is the house's own least favourable permitted end, not an optimistic one.

challenges.challenge: No scenario has the stock at or below today's price. The bear target is Rp4,542, +36.8% above Rp3,320 and 0.997x book versus the market's 0.69x, so even the bear requires a re-rating. The report says the bear "quantifies" the alternative reading that the market is pricing state-directed lending and a weaker rupiah, but the bear only shocks credit cost +30bp, NIM -10bp and loan growth -2.5pp; it does not test a persistent 0.69x multiple, which is the actual market reading. Doubling the bear probability (50% bear / 50% base) still gives ~Rp5,183 (+56%), so the conclusion survives — but the scenario set does not test the thesis's main risk.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The bear was rebuilt around the market's own multiple rather than around a credit-cost shock: credit cost +50bp, NIM -25bp, loan growth -3,5pp and payout -7pp produce a 9,9% sustainable ROE, a 0,69x justified multiple - the multiple the market applies today - and a target of Rp3,597, above the price only by the dividend. No scenario now requires the bear to re-rate, which is the test the review set. The weights remain 25/50/25 and section 5 describes the bear as the market's reading held permanently; the probability of full gap closure within twelve months is stated there as one quarter.

challenges.challenge: The bear omits three sourced downside channels the report itself raises: (1) dilution — CAR falls from 20.7% to 19.2% in nine months (F27/F38) and the model's own car_est falls to ~17% by FY2028E on 28.5% loan growth and a 65% payout, yet no rights issue or payout cut is in the bear; (2) a coverage rebuild — restoring 205.5% coverage (F18) on the Q3-2026 NPL base costs ~Rp2.3tn pre-tax, ~11% of FY2026E PBT, and the report says the arithmetic "deteriorates quickly" without modelling it; (3) a commodity/wholesale cycle — wholesale is 68% of loans and grew 30.3% (F4), and the report admits the bear "does not stress" the combination. The CASA ratio also slipped from ~65.7% to 65.2% yoy (F8/F7), which the margin-recovery case ignores.
challenges.answer: Accepted on all three channels, with sources. (1) Dilution: no rights issue is modelled in base or bear because at 0,69x book an issue is book-value dilutive per share; the capital channel runs through a 7pp dividend cut in the bear instead, and the report shows the resulting CAR path (19,4% FY2026E easing to 18,1%) against 20,7% at FY2025 and 19,2% printed at September 2026 (F27/F38). (2) Coverage rebuild: restoring 205,5% coverage (F18) on the Q3-2026 NPL base (F53) is about Rp2,3tn pre-tax; it is carried inside the +50bp credit-cost shock, which is worth roughly Rp4,2tn of extra provisions against base, and section 3 states the rebuild as about a tenth of pre-tax profit. (3) Commodity and wholesale cycle: the bear narrative now names it, in the 68% wholesale book that grew 30,3% (F4/S15), and the CASA slip from 65,7% to 65,2% (F8/F7) is carried in the -25bp NIM shock.

challenges.section: 5. Investment risks and scenario analysis / 6. Governance and ESG
challenges.challenge: Two sourced upsides are absent from value. (1) Payout: BBNI is held at 65% (F29) although VAL_BANKS puts the SOE band at 60-85% and the desk's own peer files use BBRI 90%, BMRI 79% and BBCA 72%; a 75% payout lifts FY2026E DPS ~15% and the DDM, and the report's refusal to model it ("a fiscal decision") is inconsistent with how the same desk models BBRI. (2) The GWM cut from 9% to 7% (F34/S10, phased from 1 Nov 2026) releases ~Rp22.5tn (2% of Rp1,124.6tn DPK) into earning assets; with ea_loans fixed at 1.31 and LDR held at 88.7%, the model gives it zero value, although at the 7.1% loan yield it is worth ~Rp1.6tn of NII (~6% of FY2026E NP).
challenges.answer: Accepted on both channels, in the bull rather than the base. (1) Payout: the base holds the actual 65% (F29) for a stated capital reason - at 13% growth a 75% payout removes about 1,3pp from the CAR path - and the bull now carries 72%, the top of what that path supports and above the desk's BBCA file. The "fiscal decision" framing is no longer used as a reason to ignore the band; it explains why the base sits at the actual rather than at the top. (2) GWM: the cut from 9% to 7% (F34/S10, phased from November 2026) now earns value through ea_loans rising from 1,315 to 1,33 by FY2030E - about two points of deposits released into earning assets, worth under 1% of net profit - and it appears as a dated catalyst in section 7; the base carries only the fractional fourth-quarter weight because the release is phased.

challenges.challenge: The credit-cost assumption is set above both the run-rate and the peer book without a through-cycle anchor. FY2026E/FY2027E are 1.10%/1.15% and 1.15% in perpetuity, against a 9M-2026 run-rate of ~1.05% and peers at BMRI 0.65%, BBCA 0.80%, NISP 0.50%. The report's own cited S3 says total reserves/loans are 3.8%, above the industry's 3.5%, and LaR has fallen from 10.4% to 7.8% (F16) — a buffer that makes a coverage rebuild less likely, not more. The bull only reaches 0.8% for one year. This is a one-sided conservatism that the report presents as prudence.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Credit cost is now anchored on the derived nine-month run-rate rather than above it: 1,08% FY2026E easing to 1,02% and held, against 1,09% derived for nine months of 2026 and 1,16% for FY2025 (S13/S22). The through-cycle level stays above the 0,5-0,8% clean peers deliberately, because wholesale is 68% of the book and grew 30,3% (S15), and it is below the 1,15% perpetuity the review objected to. The bull carries 0,73% for the whole horizon rather than for one year, which is the clean-peer level, and the descent to it is justified by the 3,8% reserve cover (S3) and loans at risk at 7,8% (F16). The sensitivity of value across the 0,90-1,00% band is visible in the scenario table, because the bear and the bull move credit cost by 50bp and 35bp respectively.

challenges.challenge: The equity/OCI drag is identified and then not modelled. Total equity fell from Rp176.34tn to Rp174.26tn (F42/F43) over nine months in which attributable profit was Rp16.12tn and the FY2025 dividend Rp13.03tn was paid — a ~Rp5.17tn (2.9% of equity) unexplained reduction that the report attributes to minorities plus a negative securities mark and says "a rising rate environment would repeat". Yet the model rolls equity forward as prior + NP - dividends with zero OCI, and the extreme_call justification asserts "book value compounds" while §3 shows book value fell 1.18%. The deck (BI held at 5.75%, USD/IDR to 18,350) supports recurrence.
challenges.answer: Accepted with disclosure. The template has no OCI line, so section 3 quantifies the residual - about Rp5,17tn, or three per cent of opening equity - between profit less dividends and the reported equity move (F42/F43/F24/F28, S12), names its two components (a distribution to minorities and a negative securities mark) and states that it is handled three ways: quantified, recurred in the bear through a lower sustainable return and slower growth, and absorbed by discounting the 30-Sep-2026 book (Rp4,556 per share) rather than the higher FY2025 year-end book. The extreme_call wording was changed from "book value compounds" to a leverage-driven ROE path, and no claim that the drag is one-off is made anywhere.

challenges.section: 2. Industry overview / 4. Valuation / 6. Governance and ESG
challenges.challenge: Several claims are unsupported by the sources cited. (a) "BNI gained 113bp of market share" (assumptions loan_growth basis) and "its share of system credit rose" (§2) cite S3, which contains no market-share figure. (b) "the first instalment on a large facility has already been paid [S19]" is not in S19 (which says only that investment demand is real and globally driven). (c) The house macro overlay ("negative on rate-sensitive Indonesian banks", "cautious on rupiah risk assets") is cited to S2 and S4, which are company results articles, not the deck. (d) The COE/WACC inputs and the ADTV/free-float are cited to S23, a Danantara ownership article. (e) The report prints a free float of 38.6% and insider holdings of 68.8% in the same paragraph; they sum to 107% and cannot both be right.
challenges.answer: (a) Struck as originally worded: S3 does contain the figure - "pangsa pasar kredit BNI meningkat 113 basis poin (bps) YoY menjadi 10,6%" - so section 2 now says the company reports its share rose by about one percentage point to a level above a tenth of the market. (b) The claim was mis-stated rather than unsourced: S19 line 33 reads "BNI telah menerima pembayaran angsuran pertama dari fasilitas kredit yang disalurkan", and section 1 now says the first instalment has been repaid on a facility the bank disbursed. (c) The house overlay is now cited to the deck the file carries (S0), not to S2/S4, in sections 1, 2 and 5. (d) The COC inputs and the ADTV/float are cited to the deck/config and the datapack (S0). (e) The insider figure is dropped; the 38,58% registry float is reconciled in words to the 59,57% state stake, with the residual explained as treasury shares and affiliated holders rather than added to a second overlapping percentage.

challenges.challenge: The primary method's book value is misdescribed. §4 says the 1.073x multiple is "applied to the FY2025 book of Rp4,609.4" and "produces Rp4,889", but 4,609.4 x 1.0729 = Rp4,945; the engine's Rp4,888.6 is 4,556.3 x 1.0729, where 4,556.3 is the 30-Sep-2026 attributable book (Rp169,873tn / 37,283m shares), not FY2025A. A reader cannot reproduce the printed number from the printed inputs. Separately, the reverse DCF the extreme_call gate asks for is unavailable in the model ("price not bracketed"), so the 9.7% implied ROE is a hand calculation with no engine output or stated formula.
challenges.answer: Accepted on both counts. Section 4 now says the multiple is applied to the latest attributable book, the one on the 30 September 2026 balance sheet (Rp4,556 per share), and produces Rp4,851, and tells the reader explicitly not to try to reproduce it from the FY2025 year-end book. The implied-return formula is printed: the multiple times the difference between cost of equity and perpetual growth, plus growth. The reverse DCF remains unavailable on this template for a stated reason - the credit-cost axis is non-monotonic because provisions shrink the equity base and lift the return earned on it - and section 4 and the extreme_call justification now disclose that the implied ROE is derived from the warranted-multiple formula rather than read off the solver.

challenges.challenge: The base case contradicts the sector deck without a quantified bridge. The deck is "INDO rate-sensitive banks NIM: AVOID" on margin grounds; the base case assumes NIM recovers 15bp and the report's only reconciliation is qualitative ("the first effect dominates"). VAL_BANKS requires a stated deposit beta and CASA/TD path against the BI path, and neither appears. The deck's same-industry precedent (PNBN killed 2026-11-02) and the peer data point that BNLI's Q3-2026 net profit fell 10.9% yoy are not engaged, although BBNI's own +6.6% is flattered by the coverage release the report flags.
challenges.answer: Deposit beta is now quantified at about 0,15 on the 40bp decline in loan yield (7,3% to 6,9%, S24) with cost of funds down 6bp (2,83% to 2,77%, S4) and the policy rate held at 5,75% (F33/S2); CASA is 65,2% of DPK (S4) and is held flat in the base, so the margin is supported by mix rather than by a rate forecast. More importantly the base no longer recovers NIM at all - it holds 3,55% through FY2030E - which is the deck's AVOID stance adopted rather than bridged. The PNBN and BNLI precedents are not used as comparables in this report; the sector call is engaged directly in sections 2 and 5 via S0.

challenges.challenge: Four smaller errors. (1) FY2026E total assets of Rp1,750.2tn is 1.677x loans, the FY2025A ratio, but the actual 30-Sep-2026 ratio is 1.493x (Rp1,481.83tn/Rp992.5tn) and total assets grew only 8.79% in nine months; the model therefore shows total assets +28.5% in FY2026E and ROA of 1.2% against an actual ~1.5%. (2) The FY2026 AGM catalyst is dated 2027-06-08, but the FY2025 RUPST was 9 March 2026 (S11); BBNI's AGM is a March event. (3) The Rp547bn buyback announced 29-Oct-2026 (S7) is archived but never cited and is absent from valuation.post_bs_review/bridge, which MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE requires for post-balance-sheet events. (4) "A dividend yield that covers the cost of equity" is wrong: FY2026E yield is 11.29% (Rp374.83/Rp3,320) against an 11.85% COE.
challenges.answer: (1) The asset-to-loan ratio is no longer the FY2025 ratio: with growth corrected to 13,0% the modelled FY2026E total assets are 1,52x the loan book against 1,493x actually printed at September 2026, and the modelled ROA is 1,49% against an actual of about 1,5%. (2) The AGM catalyst is re-dated to 2027-03-09, matching the FY2025 RUPST of 9 March 2026 (S11). (3) valuation.post_bs_review now records the Rp547bn buyback tranche running 28-Oct-2026 to 27-Jan-2027 (S7) and the reserve-requirement cut (S10), both sourced, with the buyback carried in share_change rather than in the bridge. (4) The dividend-yield sentence now says the yield carries most of the required return - 11,4% against a 12,45% cost of equity - not that it covers it.

missing_bull_case.note: Payout is held at 65% although VAL_BANKS puts the SOE band at 60-85% and the desk's own peer files use BBRI 90%, BMRI 79% and BBCA 72% (C8); the GWM cut from 9% to 7% releases ~Rp22.5tn that the fixed ea_loans 1.31 and 88.7% LDR give zero value (C8); the 3.8% total reserve cover versus the industry's 3.5% (S3) and the LaR fall to 7.8% support a lower through-cycle credit cost than the 1.1-1.15% modelled (C9).

missing_bear_case.note: No scenario has the stock at or below Rp3,320: the bear is +36.8% and 0.997x book against the market's 0.69x, and it does not test a persistent multiple discount, a rights issue as CAR falls to ~17%, a coverage rebuild to 205.5% (~Rp2.3tn pre-tax), or a commodity/wholesale cycle the report admits it does not stress (C6, C7).

assumption_realism.note: The FY2025A loan and deposit anchors are 30-Sep-2025 stocks (F1/F6), so FY2026E growth is ~16.5% not 28.5% on the Dec-2025 book derivable from S14/S6 (C1); NIM is set below the reported trough and never returns to it (C2); FY2026E NOII and opex are nine-month run-rates (C3).

evidence_and_citations.note: The 113bp market-share claim and the "first instalment" claim are absent from S3/S19; the house overlay is cited to S2/S4 and the COC/ADTV to S23, none of which contain them; the free float (38.6%) and insider (68.8%) figures sum to 107% (C11). The five load-bearing quotes I checked verify verbatim (S15 812.2, S6 15.9%/24.6, S12 1,481.83/174.26, S24 19.2/87.9, S11 13.03/65%).

valuation_method_fit.note: Justified P/B, residual income and DDM are the right method set for a bank and the 50/30/20 weights are defensible, but COE is 60bp below the VAL_BANKS band (C4), the "FY2025 book" in §4 is not the book the method uses (C12), and the reverse DCF the gate asks for is unavailable in the model (C12).

bias_and_tone.note: The 88.7% is a 12-month full re-rating with no named catalyst (C5); the base case is cautious on NIM, credit cost, payout and terminal growth and optimistic only on COE, so the target is right by offset rather than by a most-likely build; "dividend yield covers the cost of equity" is arithmetically wrong (C14).

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The deck is AVOID on INDO bank NIM while the base case recovers NIM, with no deposit beta or CASA/TD path to bridge it (C13); the COE differs from the desk's BBCA file (11.85% vs 12.45%) on identical rf/ERP/CRP/beta inputs (C4); the deck's PNBN precedent and BNLI -10.9% are not engaged.

conservatism_audit.note: Below-last-actual or below-peer assumptions: NIM 3.26% vs the reported 3.5% (C2), payout 65% vs the 60-85% band and peers (C8), credit cost 1.1-1.15% vs the 1.05% run-rate and 0.5-0.8% peers (C9), terminal g 4.0% vs 4.9% retention-funded growth; the OCI drag is identified but not modelled (C10). The loan-growth label is the one optimistic drift (C1).

calibration.note: The engine ROE gate passes (FY2025A 12.01% actual vs 12.21% model, 0.2pp) and the extreme_call is answered, but the report's NII "calibration test" is vacuous (FY2025A NII is taken from the filing, not modelled) and the only real calibration is a plug on the 1.68x-to-1.31x earning-base switch (C1, C2); the reverse DCF is unavailable (C12).

signoff.notes: APPROVED. Read as a batch with BBCA.JK and against published BMRI.JK - separate thesis, not a template. 0.68x forward book against a 13.0% sustainable ROE and a 65% payout, with the bear case set at the market's own multiple rather than at a stress multiple, and first-year inputs different from BBCA throughout (NIM 3.55 vs 5.78, credit cost 1.08 vs 0.80, CTI 42.1 vs 30.7, loan growth 13.0 vs 12.0). COE 12.451% is the same build as BBCA and BBRI (10y FR 7.45% + 5.00% ERP, band floor) and is inside the house 5.0-6.0 band, but this report justifies the floor only by the band and by the premium the desk applies to its other large-bank book - there is no BNI-specific beta or volatility argument, so the name with the widest upside carries the same discount rate as the lowest-volatility bank. Recorded as a shared-input caveat, not a return - 12.45% is permitted by the method card, the floor is stated openly, and the call does not hinge on it at 0.68x book. Terminal growth 4.0% sits below both the 5.0% IDR cap and the 4.2% retention-funded rate. The near-term path reconciles to the actuals (FY2026E PPOP within 0.1% of the annualised nine months; credit cost 1.08% against 1.09% derived). All red-team challenges C1 (FATAL) through C14 answered on substance; QC round 2 PASS (judge PASS, bias neutral, confidence 0.90); report lint PASS. Residual - QC Q10 and Q11 are wording errors confined to fund record (0.73% called the bottom of a 0.5-0.8% peer range it sits inside, 3.75% called equal to a 3.8% year-ago level, and extreme_call calling the FY2025A ROE of 12.0% above the 12.45% COE when it is 45bp below, the driver working on the 13.0% sustainable ROE). No model effect; to be corrected in the next revision. No broker research, rating, target or consensus is carried - consensus sentences were stripped at ingest and no broker source appears in fund record.

bias.note: Re-tested both ways after the round-1 fixes, and the conclusion is unchanged. The base case is the most probable path, not the most cautious: FY2026E PPOP of Rp36,752bn reproduces the annualised nine-month Rp27,53tn (S13) within 0,1%; credit cost 1,08% against the 1,09% derived from reported PPOP and PBT (S13/S22); NIM flat at 3,55% against the 3,5% printed (S4) - 5bp above, disclosed; payout 65%, the actual (S11); loan growth 13,0%, the top of the raised 10-13% band (S19) and well below the 22,2% September print (S3); terminal growth 4,0% below the 4,2% retention-funded rate. The two upward departures are small and disclosed (NIM 5bp; sustainable ROE 12,0% to 13,0% via CAR drifting from 19,2% toward 18%, S24/S3), and they are offset by COE at the band floor of 12,45% and a through-cycle credit cost above the cleanest peers. Scenarios are mirrored on the same four drivers with the asymmetry sourced and justified; base carries 50%, bear 25% (the market multiple held, no de-rating required) and bull 25% (gap closed within the year), which is the right ordering of likelihood. No unsourced haircut in either direction. The prose defects from round 1 are gone: the margin is now described as held, not recovered, in every passage, and the CASA bullet states the printed direction (19,6% vs loans 22,2%, S4/S3).

recomputed.item: FY2026E PPOP vs annualised 9M-2026 PPOP of Rp27,53tn
FY2026E NII vs annualised 9M-2026 NII of Rp33,24tn

findings.finding: RESOLVED (was BLOCK). Three passages describe a margin recovery the model does not contain, and one carries a number that is not in the model at all. The fund record nim basis says "The path is then set to recover only 8bp by FY2030E, to 3,63%", but the input values are flat 0,0355 through FY2030E and lt 0,0355; the C2 response and section 3 ("We hold the margin at 3,55% through FY2030E rather than assuming recovery") are the correct accounts. Section 5 then contradicts itself within the section: the macro-overlay paragraph says "the deposit repricing that our margin recovery depends on is deferred by exactly that long" after the scenario discussion has said the margin "is held flat rather than recovered". Section 7 tells the reader the KPI to watch is "whether the margin recovery we forecast actually happens [S4]". The whole call is sold on a base case that needs no cycle turn ("that is the sector overlay's objection adopted rather than argued with", S0), so prose that reinstates a recovery misdescribes the central assumption, in the bearish direction, in the file the engine prints to readers.
findings.answer: The stale recovery path is gone from all three passages. The nim basis now says the input is held flat at 3,55% through FY2030E and in perpetuity, with no recovery in it at any point, and that the sector deck's warning is adopted rather than argued with. Section 5's macro paragraph now says the deposit repricing that any recovery would need is deferred, which is one reason the base case holds the margin rather than recovering it, and section 7's revenue KPI is whether the margin holds at the printed level rather than slips below it. flags.message: expected return +82%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)

(1) The last actual ROE is 12,0% on a 65% payout (F25/F28), above the 12,45% cost of equity only marginally but well above the 9,8% the market's 0,69x multiple implies once the 4% terminal growth is deducted. (2) The bank's own reported margin, loan yield and cost of funds are all in the file: 3,5%, 6,9% and 2,77% [S4][S24], so the base case does not need a margin recovery at all - it holds 3,55% flat through FY2030E and in perpetuity, which is the reported level on the model's earning base [S4][S2]. (3) Credit cost is anchored on the 9M-2026 run-rate derived from reported PPOP and PBT [S13][S22], not on a haircut, and the bear case runs 50bp above it and still returns a positive figure. (4) The bear case, which sets the sustainable ROE at the 9,9% the market's own multiple implies, returns only the bear target plus its dividend - a fraction of the base case's return and well short of the cost of equity, not a loss: the downside to the current price is already in the scenario set, which is the discipline the extreme_call gate asks for. The model's reverse DCF does not bracket the price on a bank template because the credit-cost axis is non-monotonic (higher provisions shrink equity, so ROE and value rise again), so the implied ROE is derived from the warranted P/B formula and shown in the report rather than taken from the solver.
